scenario: 题目要求:峰值流量下,feed 排序服务要在 200ms 内返回一个个性化、够新的 feed。这是给定的产品 SLO。
scenario_en: The prompt: at peak traffic, the feed ranking service must return a personalized, fresh feed within 200ms — a given product SLO.
q: 这个 200ms 是怎么来的,它限定了哪条设计路径?
q_en: Where does the 200ms come from, and which design path does it constrain?
why: 200ms 是产品/体验给定的 SLO,不是公式推导出来的。它是总墙钟预算,要拆给检索/打分/重排三段,逼出两段式轻重打分和 fan-out 预物化,而不能在读路径上跑一个大模型算全量。
why_en: The 200ms is a given SLO, not a derived number, and it is the total wall-clock budget split across retrieval/scoring/re-ranking, forcing a two-stage light-then-heavy pipeline.
options: 200ms 是由模型总 FLOPs 除以 GPU 峰值算力精确反推出的物理下限,和产品体验无关
200ms 是给定的产品 SLO,作为总预算拆给检索/打分/重排,逼出两段式轻重打分
200ms 是网络单程物理延迟的近似值,和排序打分的计算耗时完全无关
200ms 只是监控告警阈值,超过了触发 on-call 报警,但不决定架构怎么拆分
options_en: 200ms is the physical lower bound reverse-derived by dividing total model FLOPs by peak GPU throughput, unrelated to product experience.
200ms is a given product SLO, a total budget split across retrieval/scoring/re-ranking, forcing a two-stage light-then-heavy pipeline.
200ms is roughly the one-way network physical latency, entirely unrelated to how long ranking computation takes.
200ms is just a monitoring alert threshold that pages on-call when breached, but does not decide how the architecture is split.
optionExplanations: 它不是算力推导的下限,而是产品对体验设的目标;架构要在这个目标下反推怎么排布计算。
对;200ms 是 SLO,拆成检索~30-50ms、首轮打分~50ms、重排~100ms,这个预算直接决定了必须分段、先轻后重。
网络单程只占其中一部分,200ms 是端到端墙钟预算,包含检索、打分、重排全部计算。
它既是 SLA 阈值,更是架构约束——正是因为要卡 200ms,才不得不用两段式和预物化。
optionExplanations_en: It is not a compute-derived bound but a product experience target; the architecture must lay out compute to fit it.
Correct — 200ms is an SLO split into retrieval ~30-50ms, first-pass ~50ms, re-rank ~100ms, which forces staging light-then-heavy.
One-way network is only a slice; 200ms is the end-to-end wall-clock budget covering all retrieval, scoring, and re-ranking.
It is both an SLA threshold and an architectural constraint — the 200ms cap is exactly why two-stage and pre-materialization are needed.

termDefinitions.meaning: 服务级目标,如「200ms 内返回」,是产品给定的目标而非计算推导值。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An SLO (Service Level Objective) is a target like 'respond within 200ms', given by the product rather than derived by computation.

termDefinitions.term: ranking latency budget / 排序延迟预算
termDefinitions.meaning: 每次请求的总墙钟时间(约 150-200ms),要拆分给检索、打分、重排各阶段。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The ranking latency budget is total wall-clock per request (~150-200ms), split across retrieval, scoring, and re-ranking.

scenario: feed 系统要决定:是在发帖时把帖子推进每个粉丝的时间线缓存,还是在读时才拉取合并被关注者的帖子。
scenario_en: The feed system must decide: push a post into every follower's timeline cache at publish, or fetch and merge followed accounts' posts at read time.
q: fan-out-on-write 和 fan-out-on-read 在读写代价上怎么权衡?
q_en: How do fan-out-on-write and fan-out-on-read trade off read vs write cost?
why: fan-out-on-write 发帖时就推进每个粉丝的预物化时间线,读很快,但写随粉丝数放大;fan-out-on-read 读时才拉取合并,避免了高粉账号的写放大,但读更重。权衡轴就是把成本放在写侧还是读侧。
why_en: Fan-out-on-write pre-materializes into each follower's timeline (fast reads, writes scale with followers) while fan-out-on-read merges at read time (no write amplification but heavier reads).
tradeoff: fan-out-on-write(读快、写随粉丝数放大) vs fan-out-on-read(避免写放大、读更重)
options: fan-out-on-write 读时才合并所以读慢,fan-out-on-read 发帖就推所以写重,这是把两个定义整个说反了
两者读写代价其实完全相同,只是用不用缓存的实现细节差异,和粉丝数放大无关
fan-out-on-write 发帖即推进粉丝时间线,读快写随粉丝放大;fan-out-on-read 读时才合并,避免写放大但读更重
fan-out-on-write 只适合高粉账号,fan-out-on-read 只适合普通用户,这也是把适用场景整个说反了
options_en: Fan-out-on-write merges at read time so reads are slow, and fan-out-on-read pushes at publish so writes are heavy — the definitions are fully swapped.
Both strategies actually cost the same on reads and writes; the only difference is whether a cache is used, unrelated to follower-count amplification.
Fan-out-on-write pushes into each follower timeline at publish (fast reads, writes scale with followers); fan-out-on-read merges at read time (no write amplification, heavier reads).
Fan-out-on-write suits only high-follower accounts and fan-out-on-read only normal users — the fit is also fully reversed.
optionExplanations: 定义搞反了:on-write 是发帖时推、on-read 是读时合并。
两者读写代价恰恰相反,不是仅缓存有无的区别。
对;on-write 把成本前置到写(粉丝越多写越多)、读极快;on-read 把成本放到读、避免高粉写放大,这就是权衡轴。
反了:on-write 适合普通用户(粉丝少写放大可控),on-read 适合高粉账号(避免百万级写)。
optionExplanations_en: Definitions swapped: on-write pushes at publish, on-read merges at read.
Their read/write costs are opposite, not merely a cache-presence difference.
Correct — on-write front-loads cost to writes (more followers, more writes) with instant reads; on-read shifts cost to reads and avoids high-follower write amplification.
Reversed — on-write suits normal users (few followers, bounded amplification); on-read suits high-follower accounts (avoiding millions of writes).

termDefinitions.meaning: 发帖时把帖子 ID 推进每个粉丝的预物化时间线缓存,读时直接取,读快写重。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Fan-out-on-write pushes a post into every follower's pre-materialized timeline at publish, giving fast reads and heavy writes.

termDefinitions.meaning: 读时才拉取并合并所有被关注者的帖子,避免写放大,但读更重。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Fan-out-on-read fetches and merges followed accounts' posts at read time, avoiding write amplification but making reads heavier.

scenario: 一个名人有几百万粉丝。若发一条帖就 fan-out-on-write,要往几百万个粉丝时间线写入,峰值时写队列会被打爆。
scenario_en: A celebrity has millions of followers. Fan-out-on-write on one post means millions of writes into follower timelines, blowing up the write queue at peak.
q: 高粉账号该怎么处理,普通用户又怎么处理?
q_en: How should high-follower accounts be handled, and how about normal users?
why: 按粉丝数分流:普通用户走 fan-out-on-write(写放大可控、读极快);高粉账号不推,而是放进一个高粉帖索引,读时再合并进来。这样避开百万级写放大,又保住普通用户的快读。
why_en: Split by follower count — normal users use fan-out-on-write, while high-follower accounts go into a high-follower post index merged at read time to avoid millions of writes.
tradeoff: 高粉账号 fan-out-on-write(百万级写放大、不可接受) vs 高粉帖索引读时合并(避写放大、读时多一次合并)
whenOtherWins: 如果一个账号粉丝不多、发帖也不频繁,直接 fan-out-on-write 更简单——预物化的读快收益大于那点写成本,不必进高粉索引。
diagram:
flowchart TD P["发帖"] --> C{"粉丝数?"} C -->|普通用户| W["fan-out-on-write
推进每个粉丝时间线"] C -->|高粉账号| I["高粉帖索引
读时合并"]
options: 所有账号统一 fan-out-on-write,靠加机器扛住名人的百万级写放大
普通用户 fan-out-on-write;高粉账号放进高粉帖索引、读时合并,避开百万级写放大
所有账号统一 fan-out-on-read,读时全量合并,牺牲读延迟换写简单
高粉账号 fan-out-on-write、普通用户 fan-out-on-read,按活跃度而非粉丝数分
options_en: All accounts use fan-out-on-write, absorbing a celebrity's millions of writes by adding machines.
Normal users use fan-out-on-write; high-follower accounts go into a high-follower post index merged at read time, avoiding millions of writes.
All accounts use fan-out-on-read, merging everything at read time, trading read latency for write simplicity.
High-follower accounts use fan-out-on-write and normal users fan-out-on-read, split by activity not follower count.
optionExplanations: 名人一条帖百万级写,加机器也顶不住峰值写放大,成本和尾延迟都失控。
对;混合方案让普通用户享受预物化快读,高粉账号走索引读时合并,精准避开写放大。
全 on-read 会让每次读都合并所有关注者、拖垮读延迟,普通用户没必要付这代价。
分流依据是粉丝数(写放大来源)不是活跃度,而且方向也反了。
optionExplanations_en: A celebrity post is millions of writes; adding machines cannot survive peak write amplification, and cost and tail latency spiral.
Correct — the hybrid gives normal users pre-materialized fast reads while high-follower accounts merge from an index at read time, precisely dodging amplification.
All-on-read merges every followed account on each read, tanking read latency; normal users need not pay that.
The split is by follower count (the amplification source) not activity, and the direction is also reversed.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一次发帖引发多次写入,fan-out-on-write 下写入数等于粉丝数,高粉账号可达百万级。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Write amplification is one publish causing many writes; under fan-out-on-write the count equals follower count, reaching millions for celebrities.

termDefinitions.term: high-follower post index / 高粉帖索引
termDefinitions.meaning: 存放高粉账号帖子的索引,读时再合并进粉丝 feed,避免发帖时的百万级写。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A high-follower post index stores celebrity posts to merge into feeds at read time, avoiding millions of writes at publish.

scenario: 在 200ms 预算内,feed 服务要把候选从几百个收敛到最终排序好的一屏。
scenario_en: Within the 200ms budget, the feed service must narrow candidates from a few hundred to a final ranked screen.
q: 把 200ms 内的三段式服务流程按执行顺序排列:
q_en: Order the three-stage serving pipeline that runs within 200ms:
steps: 候选检索(~30-50ms):读预物化时间线缓存 + 拉高粉帖索引,合并成几百个候选
轻量首轮打分(~50ms):蒸馏模型/逻辑回归用小特征集,裁到 top-K(50-100)
完整模型重排(~100ms):生产多任务 NN 用全特征含实时互动,产出最终列表
why: 先检索出几百个候选,再用便宜模型粗筛到 top-K(50-100),最后只对这几十个跑昂贵的多任务 NN 重排。先轻后重是为了把 200ms 里最贵的那 100ms 只花在最有希望的少数候选上。
why_en: Retrieve a few hundred candidates, cheaply trim to top-K (50-100), then run the expensive multi-task NN only on those, spending the costly 100ms only on the most promising few.
diagram:
flowchart LR R["检索 ~30-50ms
几百候选"] --> L["首轮打分 ~50ms
裁到 top-K 50-100"] L --> F["重排 ~100ms
多任务 NN 全特征"]

termDefinitions.meaning: 首轮粗筛后保留的前 K 个候选(这里 50-100),只有它们进入昂贵的重排。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Top-K is the K best candidates kept after coarse first-pass scoring (here 50-100), the only ones entering expensive re-ranking.

termDefinitions.term: multi-task NN / 多任务神经网络
termDefinitions.meaning: 同时预测点击、评论、分享等多个目标的神经网络,用于最终重排。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A multi-task neural network jointly predicts several targets (click, comment, share) and does the final re-ranking.

scenario: 三段式里,首轮打分要在约 50ms 内把几百个候选裁成 top-K(50-100),再交给昂贵的重排。
scenario_en: In the pipeline, first-pass scoring must trim a few hundred candidates to top-K (50-100) in ~50ms before the expensive re-rank.
q: 首轮打分该用什么模型和特征,为什么不用完整的多任务 NN?
q_en: What model and features should first-pass scoring use, and why not the full multi-task NN?
why: 首轮用蒸馏小模型或逻辑回归,只吃少量便宜特征(帖龄、作者亲密度、内容类型),因为要在 50ms 内给几百个候选打分。完整多任务 NN 太贵,只留给已被裁到 50-100 的候选跑,把算力花在刀刃上。
why_en: Use a distilled model or logistic regression on a small cheap feature set (post age, author affinity, content type), because scoring hundreds in 50ms rules out the expensive full NN.
tradeoff: 首轮轻量模型(快、能扫几百候选、精度略低) vs 首轮就上完整 NN(精度高但几百候选跑不完 50ms)
whenOtherWins: 如果候选池本来就很小(几十个),没必要分两段,直接用完整模型一次排完更简单也更准。
options: 直接用完整多任务 NN 打全部几百个候选,精度最高,但延迟会远超 50ms 预算
用蒸馏小模型/逻辑回归 + 少量便宜特征快速裁到 top-K,把完整 NN 留给幸存者
随机采样一半候选丢掉,剩下的直接进重排,省掉首轮打分,靠运气保留好内容
用最大的 ensemble 模型首轮打分,追求一次到位,不需要重排,但同样撑不住延迟
options_en: Run the full multi-task NN over all few hundred candidates for maximum accuracy, but latency would blow far past the 50ms budget.
Use a distilled model / logistic regression on a small cheap feature set to trim to top-K, saving the full NN for survivors.
Randomly drop half the candidates and send the rest straight to re-ranking, skipping first-pass scoring and relying on luck.
Use the largest ensemble for first-pass scoring to get it right in one shot with no re-ranking, but it equally cannot fit the budget.
optionExplanations: 完整 NN 打几百个候选在 50ms 内跑不完,直接违反延迟预算。
对;轻量模型 + 便宜特征够做粗筛,把几百裁到 50-100,再让昂贵 NN 只跑幸存者,算力用在刀刃上。
随机丢弃会误杀好候选,粗筛的意义是按信号保留最有希望的,不是靠运气。
首轮上最大 ensemble 与低延迟目标相悖,ensemble 在 serving 时正是被延迟预算排除的。
optionExplanations_en: The full NN over hundreds cannot finish in 50ms, directly violating the latency budget.
Correct — a light model plus cheap features does coarse screening, trimming hundreds to 50-100, then the costly NN runs only on survivors.
Random dropping kills good candidates; screening keeps the most promising by signal, not luck.
A large ensemble first-pass contradicts low latency; ensembles are exactly what the budget rules out at serving time.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用大模型(teacher)的知识训练出的小模型,推理便宜,适合首轮快速打分。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A distilled model is a small model trained from a large teacher's knowledge, cheap to infer, ideal for fast first-pass scoring.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用户与某作者历史互动的紧密程度,是便宜且有区分度的首轮特征。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Author affinity is how strongly a user has historically interacted with an author, a cheap and discriminative first-pass feature.

scenario: 为了让 feed 够新,系统用一个异步重排 worker 监听实时互动流,而不是每次读都跑整条三段式流水线。
scenario_en: For freshness, an async re-ranking worker listens to a real-time engagement stream instead of running the full pipeline on every read.
q: 近实时重排是怎么工作的,为什么不在每次读时重跑全流水线?
q_en: How does near-real-time re-ranking work, and why not re-run the full pipeline on every read?
why: 异步 worker 订阅实时互动流,几秒内把新帖/新互动刷新进缓存的时间线,读请求直接取已刷新的结果。每次读都重跑三段式会烧掉算力且撑爆延迟预算,近实时刷新把更新和读解耦。
why_en: An async worker subscribes to the engagement stream and refreshes cached timelines within seconds, so reads serve the refreshed result instead of re-running the whole pipeline each time.
options: 每次读都同步重跑三段式流水线,保证绝对最新,不用缓存,但峰值 QPS 下扛不住
异步 worker 订阅实时互动流,几秒内刷新缓存时间线,读时直接取,更新与读解耦
定时每小时批量重排一次,读时永远取上小时的快照,新鲜度明显跟不上
让客户端自己在本地重排,服务端不做任何近实时更新,拿不到全量互动信号
options_en: Synchronously re-run the full pipeline on every read for absolute freshness with no cache, but it cannot survive peak QPS.
An async worker subscribes to the engagement stream and refreshes the cached timeline within seconds, so reads serve it — decoupling update from read.
Batch re-rank once per hour, and reads always serve the previous hour snapshot, clearly failing freshness.
Have the client re-rank locally, with the server doing no near-real-time updates, so it never sees the full engagement signal.
optionExplanations: 每次读同步重跑会烧算力、撑爆 200ms 预算,峰值下根本扛不住 QPS。
对;异步 worker 在后台按互动流刷新缓存,读请求只做取用,既新鲜又不违反延迟预算。
每小时批量太慢,feed 会明显过时,达不到「够新」的要求。
客户端本地重排拿不到全量实时互动信号,也无法保证一致,近实时更新应在服务端。
optionExplanations_en: Synchronous re-run per read burns compute and blows the 200ms budget, failing at peak QPS.
Correct — an async worker refreshes the cache from the engagement stream in the background, and reads just serve it: fresh without breaking the budget.
Hourly batch is too slow; the feed goes visibly stale, failing the freshness requirement.
Client-side re-ranking lacks full real-time engagement signals and consistency; near-real-time updates belong on the server.

termDefinitions.meaning: 异步 worker 监听实时互动流,几秒内刷新缓存时间线,而非每次读重跑全流水线。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Near-real-time re-ranking uses an async worker on the engagement stream to refresh cached timelines within seconds, not per-read.

termDefinitions.meaning: 承载点赞、评论、点击等实时互动事件的消息流,供重排 worker 订阅。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The engagement stream is a message stream of real-time likes, comments, and clicks that the re-ranking worker subscribes to.

scenario: 流量突增,fan-out-on-write 的分发队列开始积压:帖子已提交但堆在队列里没分发出去。所有服务的 p99 延迟、错误率看着都正常。
scenario_en: Traffic spikes and the fan-out-on-write queue backs up: posts are submitted but sit undistributed. Every service's p99 latency and error rate look healthy.
q: 这个首要故障模式为什么危险,唯一可靠的发现手段是什么?
q_en: Why is this primary failure mode dangerous, and what is the only reliable way to catch it?
why: 危险在于系统看着健康(延迟/错误率都正常),但用户看到的是过时 feed——新帖卡在队列里没推到时间线。唯一可靠的捕捉是监控队列深度:队列积压是这个「静默过时」的直接信号。
why_en: It is dangerous because the system looks healthy (latency and errors normal) while users see stale feeds, and monitoring fan-out queue depth is the only reliable catch.
diagram:
flowchart LR P["发帖提交"] --> Q["fan-out 队列
积压"] Q -.卡住.-> T["粉丝时间线
未更新"] T --> U["用户看到过时 feed"] Q --> D["队列深度监控
唯一可靠信号"]
options: 危险在延迟飙升,靠 p99 latency 报警就能发现,报警一响就知道要处理
危险在系统看着健康、用户却见过时 feed,只有监控队列深度能可靠捕捉
危险在错误率上升,靠 5xx 计数就能发现,一看错误率曲线就清楚
危险在缓存命中率下降,靠命中率监控就能发现,命中率一跌就报警
options_en: The danger is latency spiking, and p99 latency alerts catch it the moment they fire.
The danger is the system looks healthy while users see stale feeds, and only monitoring queue depth reliably catches it.
The danger is error rate rising, and 5xx counts catch it as soon as the curve moves.
The danger is cache hit rate dropping, and hit-rate monitoring pages the moment it falls.
optionExplanations: 正因为延迟没飙升,p99 报警完全不会触发,这才是它隐蔽的原因。
对;积压不改变在线延迟/错误率,系统「看起来正常」,只有队列深度暴露新帖没被分发这个真相。
错误率也不升,请求都成功返回,只是返回的是旧内容,5xx 抓不到。
缓存照常命中(命中的是旧时间线),命中率监控看不出内容已过时。
optionExplanations_en: Precisely because latency does not spike, p99 alerts never fire — that is why it hides.
Correct — a backlog does not change online latency/errors, so the system 'looks fine'; only queue depth reveals undistributed posts.
Error rate does not rise either; requests succeed but return stale content, so 5xx misses it.
The cache still hits (on the stale timeline), so hit-rate monitoring cannot see the content is outdated.

termDefinitions.term: queue depth monitoring / 队列深度监控
termDefinitions.meaning: 跟踪 fan-out 分发队列里积压的消息数,是捕捉「静默过时 feed」的唯一可靠信号。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Queue depth monitoring tracks pending messages in the fan-out queue, the only reliable signal for silently stale feeds.

termDefinitions.meaning: 99 分位延迟:99% 的请求比这个值快,反映尾部最慢那批用户的体验。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: p99 latency is the 99th-percentile response time — 99% of requests are faster — reflecting the slowest tail users' experience.

scenario: 监控显示 fan-out 队列深度 >10K 积压、用户报告 feed 过时,但完整重排模型的 p99 延迟仍在 SLA 之内。
scenario_en: Monitoring shows fan-out queue depth >10K and users report stale feeds, but the full re-ranker's p99 latency is still within SLA.
q: 该先动哪里?
q_en: Where should you act first?
why: 瓶颈在 fan-out 不在模型:模型 p99 正常说明排序算得动,问题是新帖卡在分发队列没进时间线。该扩 fan-out worker、并对「过时 feed 率」告警,而不是去动没问题的排序模型。
why_en: The bottleneck is fan-out, not the model — the re-ranker's p99 is fine, so scale up fan-out workers and alert on stale-feed rate rather than touching the healthy model.
tradeoff: 扩 fan-out worker(治真瓶颈、消积压) vs 优化排序模型(模型没问题、白费力)
whenOtherWins: 如果是模型 p99 超过 200ms 而队列深度正常,那瓶颈才在模型侧,该降级到轻量打分器或缩小候选集。
options: 扩容重排模型的 GPU,因为 feed 过时一定是排序太慢,先加卡再说
扩 fan-out worker 并对过时 feed 率告警,因为瓶颈在分发不在模型
回滚排序模型到上一版本,先止血再排查,反正模型换个版本总没错,不管队列堆没堆积
提高缓存 TTL,让旧 feed 缓存更久以减压,先把队列压力糊过去
options_en: Scale up the re-ranker GPUs, since stale feeds must mean ranking is too slow — add cards first.
Scale up fan-out workers and alert on stale-feed rate, because the bottleneck is distribution, not the model.
Roll back the ranking model to the previous version to stop the bleeding first, on the theory any rollback is safe, regardless of whether the queue is backed up.
Raise the cache TTL so stale feeds cache longer to relieve pressure, papering over the queue backlog.
optionExplanations: 模型 p99 在 SLA 内说明排序不慢,扩 GPU 治不了积压的分发队列,是找错了地方。
对;队列 >10K + 模型 p99 正常,明确指向 fan-out 分发瓶颈,扩 worker 消积压并对过时率告警才对症。
回滚模型无济于事,模型本来就健康,过时源自队列积压。
调高 TTL 只会让用户看到更旧的内容,是掩盖症状不是治瓶颈。
optionExplanations_en: The model's p99 within SLA means ranking is not slow; scaling GPUs cannot clear a backed-up distribution queue — wrong target.
Correct — queue >10K with a healthy model p99 points squarely at the fan-out bottleneck, so scale workers and alert on stale rate.
Rolling back the model helps nothing; the model is healthy and staleness comes from the queue backlog.
Raising TTL just serves even older content, masking the symptom rather than fixing the bottleneck.

termDefinitions.term: fan-out worker / 分发工作进程
termDefinitions.meaning: 负责把新帖推进各粉丝时间线的后台进程,积压时可水平扩容来消化队列。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A fan-out worker is a background process pushing new posts into follower timelines, scaled horizontally to drain a backlog.

scenario: 一个排序模型不是突然崩,而是 CTR 每天悄悄跌 0.3%,没有任何单一硬阈值被击穿。
scenario_en: A ranking model does not crash; CTR quietly drops 0.3% per day with no single hard threshold ever breached.
q: 这种静默退化为什么难抓,该用什么监控?
q_en: Why is this silent degradation hard to catch, and what monitoring catches it?
why: 静默退化每天只跌一点、不触发任何硬阈值,盯单点阈值的告警看不见。要监控预测分数分布的漂移:把每小时打分直方图和 24 小时基线比,能提前抓到重训回归或特征管线故障导致的分布偏移。
why_en: Each day's tiny drop breaches no hard threshold, so threshold alerts miss it; monitor prediction score-distribution drift (hourly histogram vs 24h baseline) to catch it.
options: 靠 p99 延迟阈值,延迟没变就说明模型没退化,盯着延迟曲线就够了
靠单一 CTR 硬阈值告警,跌破就报警,每天只跌一点永远不会触发
监控预测分数分布漂移:每小时直方图对比 24h 基线,抓分布偏移与重训回归
只看总请求量,量没跌就说明模型健康,量稳定时质量照样能烂掉
options_en: Rely on p99 latency thresholds; if latency is unchanged, watching the latency curve alone is enough to call the model healthy.
Rely on a single hard CTR threshold alert that fires on breach, but a tiny daily drop never trips it at all.
Monitor prediction score-distribution drift: hourly histogram vs a 24h baseline to catch distribution shift and retraining regressions.
Watch only total request volume; if volume holds, the model must be healthy, even while quality quietly rots.
optionExplanations: 延迟和模型质量退化无关,静默退化不会体现在延迟上。
单一硬阈值正是抓不到的原因——每天 0.3% 永远不会一次性击穿阈值。
对;分布漂移监控看的是形状变化而非单点越界,能在硬阈值被击穿前发现重训回归或特征故障。
请求量不反映排序质量,量稳定时 CTR 照样能慢慢烂掉。
optionExplanations_en: Latency is unrelated to quality degradation; silent decay does not show up in latency.
A single hard threshold is exactly why it is missed — 0.3% a day never breaches at once.
Correct — distribution-drift monitoring watches shape change, not a point breach, catching retraining regressions before any threshold trips.
Request volume does not reflect ranking quality; CTR can rot slowly while volume stays flat.

termDefinitions.term: score distribution drift / 分数分布漂移
termDefinitions.meaning: 模型输出分数的分布随时间偏离基线,常由重训回归或特征管线故障引起。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Score distribution drift is the model's output-score distribution moving away from baseline over time, often from retraining regressions or feature-pipeline failures.

scenario: 你要给 feed 排序搭一套三层监控,从系统健康一直看到业务生态。
scenario_en: You are building a three-layer monitoring stack for feed ranking, from system health to business ecosystem.
q: 这三层监控各看什么?
q_en: What does each of the three monitoring layers watch?
why: 三层各司其职:基建看延迟/队列/缓存/QPS,模型健康看分数漂移/特征新鲜度/null 率,业务看 unfollow/留存/创作者激活(7 天滚动窗)。
why_en: Infra watches latency/queue/cache/QPS, model health watches score drift/feature freshness/null rate, and business watches unfollow/retention/creator activation on 7-day windows.
options: 基建层看分数漂移、模型层看延迟、业务层看 CPU 使用率和内存占用,这是把三层的核心指标整个错配,谁都对不上号
基建看延迟/队列/缓存/QPS,模型健康看分数漂移/特征新鲜度/null 率,业务看 unfollow/留存/创作者激活
三层都只看 CTR,分别按分钟/小时/天聚合出三条一样的曲线,退化成单一指标反复看,看不出任何分层信息
基建看营收数字、模型看点击总数、业务看服务器数量和机房温度,三层量各归各错,完全没对上号
options_en: Infra watches score drift, model watches latency, and business watches CPU usage and memory — the layers and metrics are entirely mismatched, none lining up.
Infra watches latency/queue/cache/QPS, model health watches score drift/feature freshness/null rate, business watches unfollow/retention/creator activation.
All three watch only CTR, aggregated per minute/hour/day into three identical curves, reverting to one metric viewed three times with no layer-specific signal.
Infra watches revenue, model watches total clicks, business watches server count and datacenter temperature — every layer is paired with the wrong quantity.
optionExplanations: 层与指标错配:分数漂移属模型层、延迟属基建层,写反了。
对;基建管系统健康、模型管预测健康、业务管生态健康,三层各司其职、互不替代。
只看 CTR 就退回单指标监控,看不到延迟、漂移、创作者生态等不同层的问题。
营收/服务器数不是这三层的核心量,层与指标完全错位。
optionExplanations_en: Layers and metrics mismatched: score drift belongs to the model layer, latency to infra — reversed.
Correct — infra covers system health, model covers prediction health, business covers ecosystem health; each is distinct and non-substitutable.
Watching only CTR reverts to single-metric monitoring, missing latency, drift, and creator-ecosystem issues across layers.
Revenue/server count are not these layers' core quantities; layers and metrics are entirely misaligned.

termDefinitions.meaning: 特征值距上次更新有多久,过时特征会让模型基于旧信息打分而悄悄退化。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Feature freshness is how recently a feature was updated; stale features make the model score on old information and degrade quietly.

termDefinitions.term: creator activation rate / 创作者激活率
termDefinitions.meaning: 创作者持续发帖/活跃的比例,反映内容供给侧生态健康。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Creator activation rate is the share of creators who keep posting and stay active, reflecting supply-side ecosystem health.

scenario: 线上给模型打分分布配了自动回滚:每小时算当前分数分布和 24 小时基线的差异,超阈值就自动回滚到上一版模型。
scenario_en: Production auto-rollback compares the current score distribution to a 24h baseline hourly and rolls back if it diverges past a threshold.
q: 用什么量衡量这个分布差异,阈值大概设在哪、触发后怎么办?
q_en: What measures this divergence, roughly what threshold, and what happens on trigger?
why: 用 KL 散度衡量当前分数分布相对 24h 基线的偏离,经验阈值约 >0.05 就自动回滚到上一版模型。这是自动止血:分布突变往往是重训回归或特征管线故障,先回滚再排查根因。
why_en: Use KL divergence of the current score distribution vs the 24h baseline, and a rule-of-thumb >0.05 triggers auto-rollback to the previous model.
options: 用准确率衡量,低于 90% 就回滚,但准确率需要标签、根本拿不到实时值
用 KL 散度衡量分布偏离,经验阈值约 >0.05 就自动回滚到上一版模型
用 p99 延迟衡量,超 200ms 就回滚模型,但延迟和分数分布是两回事
用 CTR 绝对值衡量,跌破历史均值就回滚,但季节和流量波动会天天误报
options_en: Measure with accuracy, roll back below 90% — but accuracy needs labels and is never available in real time.
Measure distribution divergence with KL divergence; a rule-of-thumb >0.05 auto-rolls back to the previous model.
Measure with p99 latency, roll back the model above 200ms — but latency and score distribution are unrelated signals.
Measure with absolute CTR, roll back when it drops below the historical mean, but seasonality and traffic noise would false-page daily.
optionExplanations: 准确率需要标签、有延迟,拿不到实时;这里要的是无标签就能算的分布偏离量。
对;KL 散度比较两个分布的距离,>0.05(经验阈值)触发自动回滚,先止血再查是重训回归还是特征故障。
延迟是基建层信号,和分数分布漂移是两回事,不该用来触发模型回滚。
CTR 绝对值受季节/流量波动干扰大,不如无标签的分布漂移灵敏且及时。
optionExplanations_en: Accuracy needs labels and is delayed, unavailable in real time; here you want a label-free distribution divergence.
Correct — KL divergence compares two distributions' distance, and >0.05 (rule of thumb) triggers auto-rollback to stop the bleeding before root-causing.
Latency is an infra signal, distinct from score-distribution drift, and should not trigger a model rollback.
Absolute CTR is noisy from seasonality/traffic; label-free distribution drift is more sensitive and timely.

termDefinitions.meaning: 衡量两个概率分布差异的量,这里比较当前分数分布和 24h 基线,>0.05 触发回滚。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: KL (Kullback-Leibler) divergence measures the gap between two distributions, here current scores vs a 24h baseline, with >0.05 triggering rollback.

termDefinitions.meaning: 监控指标越界时自动切回上一个已知良好模型版本,先止血后排查。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Auto-rollback automatically reverts to the last known-good model version when a monitored metric breaches, stopping harm before diagnosis.

scenario: 监控发现某个 top-10 重要特征的 null 率突然涨到超过 2%。
scenario_en: Monitoring shows a top-10 feature's null rate suddenly climbs past 2%.
q: 这通常意味着什么,该触发什么动作?
q_en: What does this usually mean, and what action should it trigger?
why: 重要特征 null 率飙升几乎总是上游特征管线出故障(数据源挂了、ETL 失败),模型只能拿缺失值打分、质量悄悄崩。动作:阻断本次模型更新并告警数据管线团队,先堵住坏特征进模型,再修上游。
why_en: A spiking null rate on a key feature almost always means an upstream feature-pipeline failure, so block the model update and alert the data-pipeline team.
options: 意味着用户变少了,应扩容服务器,但用户数和特征缺失完全是两件事
意味着上游特征管线故障,应阻断本次模型更新并告警数据管线团队
意味着模型过拟合,应立即重训一版,但过拟合不会表现成线上 null 率
意味着缓存过期,应清空缓存重建,但清缓存治不了特征值本身缺失
options_en: It means fewer users; scale up servers — but user count and missing features are unrelated problems.
It means an upstream feature-pipeline failure; block the model update and alert the data-pipeline team.
It means the model overfits; immediately retrain — but overfitting never shows up as a live null-rate spike.
It means the cache expired; flush and rebuild the cache — but a flush cannot fix values that are genuinely missing.
optionExplanations: null 率是特征质量信号,和用户数无关,扩容治不了缺失特征。
对;重要特征突然大量缺失指向上游数据源/ETL 故障,先阻断更新防坏特征进模型,再让数据团队修根因。
过拟合是训练问题,不会表现为线上特征 null 率突增,重训也不修上游故障。
缓存过期不会导致特征值为 null,清缓存无关这个数据管线故障。
optionExplanations_en: Null rate is a feature-quality signal unrelated to user count; scaling cannot fix missing features.
Correct — a key feature suddenly missing points to an upstream source/ETL failure; block the update to keep bad features out, then have data fix the root cause.
Overfitting is a training issue, not a live null-rate spike, and retraining does not fix an upstream failure.
Cache expiry does not null out feature values; flushing the cache is unrelated to this pipeline failure.

termDefinitions.meaning: 某特征取值为缺失/空的样本比例,突增通常暴露上游特征管线故障。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Null rate is the share of samples where a feature is missing; a spike usually exposes an upstream feature-pipeline failure.

scenario: 监控的业务结果层要在 7 天滚动窗上看 feed 排序对用户和创作者生态的长期影响。
scenario_en: The business-outcome layer watches feed ranking's long-term impact on the user and creator ecosystem on rolling 7-day windows.
q: 以下哪些属于业务结果层该监控的指标?(多选)
q_en: Which belong to the business-outcome monitoring layer? (multiple)
why: 业务结果层看关系和生态:unfollow 率、28 天留存、创作者激活率、创作者曝光 Gini,都在 7 天滚动窗上跑。推理 QPS 是基建层的吞吐信号,不属于业务结果。
why_en: The business layer watches relationships and ecosystem — unfollow rate, 28-day retention, creator activation, creator-impression Gini — on 7-day windows, while inference QPS is an infra metric.
options: unfollow 率——用户与创作者的关系流失
28 天留存——长期用户健康
创作者激活率与创作者曝光 Gini——供给侧生态健康与曝光公平
推理 QPS——每秒模型打分次数
options_en: Unfollow rate — user-creator relationship loss.
28-day retention — long-term user health.
Creator activation rate and creator-impression Gini — supply-side ecosystem health and exposure fairness.
Inference QPS — model scores per second.
optionExplanations: 对;unfollow 是关系流失的直接业务信号,7 天窗上看趋势。
对;28 天留存是长期用户健康的黄金指标,属业务结果层。
对;创作者激活率和曝光 Gini 守住供给侧生态,是业务层不可少的创作者视角。
错;推理 QPS 是基建层吞吐信号,反映系统压力而非业务生态结果。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — unfollow is a direct relationship-loss business signal, trended on a 7-day window.
Correct — 28-day retention is the gold long-term user-health metric, a business-layer concern.
Correct — creator activation and impression Gini guard supply-side ecosystem, the essential creator view at the business layer.
Wrong — inference QPS is an infra throughput signal reflecting system load, not a business-ecosystem outcome.

termDefinitions.meaning: 始终取最近 7 天数据聚合,平滑日间波动、看出中期趋势。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A rolling 7-day window always aggregates the last 7 days to smooth daily noise and reveal medium-term trends.

scenario: 完整重排模型突然大量报错/超时,再等它恢复,用户就刷不出 feed 了。你要立刻止血。
scenario_en: The full re-ranker suddenly errors/times out en masse; waiting for recovery means users get no feed. You must stop the bleeding now.
q: 立即处置该怎么做?
q_en: What is the immediate response?
why: 立即处置两手:一是自动回滚到上一个已知良好 checkpoint;二是若完整排序器不健康,优雅降级到轻量首轮打分器——质量降一档但 feed 不断流。核心是先保可用,再中期排根因。
why_en: Auto-roll back to the last known-good checkpoint, and if the full ranker is unhealthy, gracefully degrade to the lightweight first-pass scorer so feeds keep flowing at lower quality.
tradeoff: 降级到轻量打分器(质量降一档但 feed 不断) vs 死等完整模型恢复(质量满但用户刷不出 feed)
whenOtherWins: 如果只是单次坏 checkpoint 上线、轻量打分器同样受影响,那直接回滚到上一版模型比降级更对症。
options: 停服等工程师查明根因后再恢复,避免降质,但用户直接刷不出 feed,可用性直接归零
自动回滚到已知良好 checkpoint;完整排序器不健康时降级到轻量首轮打分器,保 feed 不断流
把所有请求排队等完整模型恢复,宁慢不降质,结果延迟爆炸、请求堆积,用户照样刷不出 feed 来
直接关掉排序,给所有人按时间倒序展示,永久用这个兜底,放弃个性化,长期体验持续受损
options_en: Take the service down until engineers root-cause, avoiding any quality drop — but users get no feed at all and availability hits zero.
Auto-roll back to a known-good checkpoint; if the full ranker is unhealthy, degrade to the lightweight first-pass scorer to keep feeds flowing.
Queue all requests waiting for the full model to recover — slow but no quality loss — yet latency explodes, requests pile up, and users still see nothing.
Turn off ranking and show everyone reverse-chronological permanently as the fallback, abandoning personalization and hurting experience for the long haul.
optionExplanations: 停服是最差止血,用户直接刷不出 feed,可用性归零。
对;先回滚到已知良好版本,不行就降级到轻量打分器,牺牲一档质量换 feed 持续可用,再中期查根因。
排队死等会让延迟爆炸、请求堆积,同样导致用户刷不出,不是止血。
永久退回时间倒序放弃了个性化,是长期损失;降级应是临时兜底而非永久方案。
optionExplanations_en: Taking the service down is the worst stop-gap; users get no feed and availability hits zero.
Correct — roll back to known-good, and if needed degrade to the light scorer, trading one quality tier for continuous availability, then root-cause.
Queuing and waiting explodes latency and piles up requests, also leaving users without a feed — not a fix.
Permanent reverse-chronological abandons personalization for a long-term loss; degradation should be a temporary fallback, not permanent.

termDefinitions.meaning: 主组件故障时退到更简单但仍可用的组件(如轻量打分器),牺牲质量保可用。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Graceful degradation falls back to a simpler but still-working component (e.g. the light scorer) when the main one fails, trading quality for availability.

termDefinitions.term: known-good checkpoint / 已知良好检查点
termDefinitions.meaning: 此前验证过健康、可随时回滚到的模型版本快照。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A known-good checkpoint is a previously verified-healthy model snapshot you can roll back to at any time.

scenario: 止血之后进入中期处置,你要系统性地定位 feed 排序退化的根因。
scenario_en: After stopping the bleeding, the medium-term step is to systematically root-cause the ranking degradation.
q: 退化的根因通常落在哪三类?
q_en: Which three categories does the root cause usually fall into?
why: 三类根因:特征管线故障(特征过时/为 null)、数据分布漂移(如某类内容突然刷屏改变了输入分布)、模型回归(某次训练跑坏了但离线评估没抓到)。分门别类才能对症修复。
why_en: Three categories — feature-pipeline failure (stale/null), data distribution shift (a viral event flooding one content type), and model regression (a bad training run passing offline evaluation).
options: 特征管线故障、数据分布漂移、模型回归
服务器过热、网络抖动、磁盘写满
用户流失、营收下降、竞品上线
缓存击穿、DNS 解析失败、证书过期
options_en: Feature-pipeline failure, data distribution shift, model regression.
Server overheating, network jitter, disk full.
User churn, revenue decline, competitor launch.
Cache breakdown, DNS failure, certificate expiry.
optionExplanations: 对;这三类覆盖了模型退化的主要来源——输入坏(特征)、世界变(分布)、模型坏(回归),排查按此分流。
这些是通用基建故障,不针对排序模型质量退化,方向太泛。
这些是业务结果不是技术根因,回答不了「模型为什么变差」。
这些是网络/基建可用性故障,和排序模型的质量退化不是一类问题。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — these three cover the main sources of model degradation: bad inputs (features), a changed world (distribution), a broken model (regression).
These are generic infra failures, not specific to ranking-model quality degradation — too broad.
These are business outcomes, not technical root causes, and cannot explain why the model got worse.
These are network/infra availability failures, a different class from ranking-model quality degradation.

termDefinitions.term: data distribution shift / 数据分布漂移
termDefinitions.meaning: 线上输入分布偏离训练分布(如病毒事件让某类内容暴增),使模型预测失准。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Data distribution shift is live input drifting from training (e.g. a viral event flooding one content type), throwing off predictions.

termDefinitions.meaning: 某次训练产出更差的模型却通过了离线评估,上线后才暴露质量下降。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Model regression is a training run producing a worse model that passed offline eval, revealing degradation only in production.

scenario: 你想让 feed 更新鲜,于是提高近实时重排的频率,但工程师担心成本和尾延迟。
scenario_en: You want a fresher feed so you raise near-real-time re-ranking frequency, but engineers worry about cost and tail latency.
q: 新鲜度和延迟这个 dial 怎么权衡?
q_en: How does the freshness-vs-latency dial trade off?
why: 这是个连续 dial 不是开关:异步重排越频繁,feed 越新,但消耗更多算力、推高尾延迟(p99)和队列深度。要看着队列深度和 p99 去调这个旋钮,而不是一味求新。
why_en: It is a continuous dial — more async re-ranking means fresher feeds but more compute, higher tail latency, and deeper queues, tuned by watching queue depth and p99.
tradeoff: 重排更频繁(更新鲜) vs 更省算力/更低尾延迟(但稍旧)——看队列深度和 p99 调 dial
options: 新鲜度和延迟无关,可以同时拉满两者,不用看队列深度或 p99 这些监控指标
重排越频繁 feed 越新,但更耗算力、推高 p99 和队列深度,要看这两个指标调旋钮
只要加缓存就能同时做到最新鲜和最低延迟,没有权衡,权衡就此彻底消失不用再调
延迟只由网络决定,重排频率再高也不影响延迟,和算力、队列压力都无关
options_en: Freshness and latency are unrelated; you can max both at once without ever watching queue depth or p99.
More re-ranking means fresher feeds but more compute, higher p99, and deeper queues, tuned by watching those two.
Just add cache and you get both maximum freshness and minimum latency, no trade-off left, and the dial never needs tuning again.
Latency is set only by the network; re-ranking frequency does not affect it, unrelated to compute or queue pressure.
optionExplanations: 两者恰恰互相牵制,越追新鲜越费算力、越推高尾延迟,不能同时拉满。
对;这是连续 dial:频率↑→新鲜↑但算力/p99/队列↑,靠监控队列深度和 p99 找平衡点。
加缓存缓解读延迟,但更频繁的重排本身增加计算和尾延迟,权衡依然存在。
重排频率直接决定计算量和队列压力,进而影响 p99,不只是网络决定延迟。
optionExplanations_en: They constrain each other — chasing freshness costs compute and raises tail latency, so you cannot max both.
Correct — a continuous dial: higher frequency lifts freshness but also compute/p99/queue, balanced by watching queue depth and p99.
Cache eases read latency, but more frequent re-ranking itself adds compute and tail latency, so the trade-off remains.
Re-ranking frequency drives compute and queue pressure and thus p99; latency is not set by the network alone.

termDefinitions.meaning: 新鲜度与延迟的连续权衡:重排越勤越新但越费算力、尾延迟越高,是可调旋钮非开关。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The freshness-vs-latency dial is a continuous trade-off: more re-ranking means fresher but costlier and higher-tail-latency, a knob not a switch.

scenario: 你想上一个更大的排序模型提升质量,但更大的模型推理更慢,可能击穿 200ms 的 p99 SLA。
scenario_en: You want a bigger ranking model for quality, but bigger means slower inference that may breach the 200ms p99 SLA.
q: 模型复杂度和服务预算这个 dial 怎么管?
q_en: How do you manage the model-complexity-vs-serving-budget dial?
why: 更大模型质量更好但更慢、易撑破 p99 SLA。用蒸馏(把大模型知识压进小模型)加两段式流水线来管这个 dial:让轻量首轮扫全量、只有 top-K 才跑重模型,在预算内拿到接近大模型的质量。
why_en: Bigger models give quality but risk the p99 SLA, so distillation plus a two-stage pipeline manage the dial — light scorer over all, heavy model only on top-K.
tradeoff: 更大模型(质量高但慢、险破 p99) vs 蒸馏+两段式(质量接近但守住延迟预算)
options: 无脑上最大模型,延迟问题靠加机器无限扩容解决,反正预算无上限
更大模型质量高但险破 p99,用蒸馏+两段式:轻量扫全量、重模型只跑 top-K
永远只用最小模型,牺牲质量换绝对低延迟,不做任何两段式,放弃质量上限
模型大小和延迟无关,选多大都不影响 p99,加卡也白加
options_en: Always ship the biggest model and solve latency by scaling machines infinitely, as if budget were unlimited.
Bigger models raise quality but risk p99, so use distillation plus two-stage: light scorer over all, heavy model only on top-K.
Always use the smallest model, sacrificing quality for absolute low latency, with no two-stage — forfeiting the quality ceiling.
Model size is unrelated to latency; any size leaves p99 unchanged, so adding GPUs would be pointless.
optionExplanations: 加机器降不了单请求的模型推理时间,p99 该破还是破,成本还爆炸。
对;蒸馏压缩计算、两段式让重模型只碰 top-K,既逼近大模型质量又守住 200ms 预算。
一味用最小模型放弃了质量上限,两段式本可在预算内兼顾质量,没必要走极端。
模型越大单次推理越慢,直接影响 p99,大小与延迟强相关。
optionExplanations_en: Adding machines does not cut per-request inference time; p99 still breaches and cost explodes.
Correct — distillation shrinks compute and two-stage runs the heavy model only on top-K, approaching big-model quality within the 200ms budget.
Always-smallest forfeits the quality ceiling; two-stage can balance both within budget, so the extreme is unnecessary.
Bigger models infer slower per request, directly affecting p99 — size strongly correlates with latency.

termDefinitions.meaning: 单请求可用的延迟/算力上限,模型复杂度必须被它约束住。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The serving budget is the per-request latency/compute ceiling that model complexity must fit within.

scenario: 有人提议从「按用户各自时间线打分(local)」切换到「跨全平台内容统一打分(global)」以提升相关性。
scenario_en: A proposal switches from scoring within each user's timeline (local) to scoring across all platform content (global) for relevance.
q: 全局排序 vs 局部排序这个 dial,风险在哪?
q_en: For the global-vs-local ranking dial, where is the risk?
why: 全局排序常能提升相关性,但会把曝光分布推离小众创作者、拉高创作者 Gini,伤害多样性和公平——这是个带公平色彩的内容分发决策,不是纯技术开关。用创作者激活率来监测这种伤害。
why_en: Global ranking often lifts relevance but shifts impressions away from niche creators, raising Gini and harming fairness — a fairness-laden distribution decision, watched via creator activation rate.
tradeoff: 全局排序(相关性↑但曝光离开小众、Gini↑) vs 局部排序(多样性稳但相关性略低)
whenOtherWins: 如果平台正苦于内容同质、用户抱怨看不到全站好内容,且创作者 Gini 有余量,那切向全局排序换相关性是值得的。
options: 全局排序纯提升相关性,没有任何副作用,应无条件切换,不用看任何生态指标
全局排序提升相关性但把曝光推离小众创作者、拉高 Gini,是带公平色彩的分发决策
全局和局部排序结果完全一样,切换没意义,不影响相关性也不影响曝光
全局排序只影响延迟不影响曝光分布,是纯性能问题,和创作者公平无关
options_en: Global ranking purely improves relevance with no side effects at all, so switch unconditionally and skip watching any ecosystem metric.
Global ranking lifts relevance but shifts impressions away from niche creators and raises Gini — a fairness-laden distribution decision.
Global and local ranking give identical results, so switching is pointless — no change to relevance or exposure.
Global ranking affects only latency, not exposure distribution — a pure performance issue unrelated to creator fairness.
optionExplanations: 「无副作用」正是陷阱:全局排序会系统性地把曝光从小众挪向热门,损害多样性和公平。
对;相关性和创作者公平在这里对立,切全局要盯着 Gini 和创作者激活率,把它当分发决策而非纯技术选择。
两者结果不同——全局在更大候选集上比较,分布会明显偏移。
全局排序的核心影响是曝光分布(公平),不只是延迟,把它当纯性能问题会漏掉公平风险。
optionExplanations_en: 'No side effects' is the trap: global ranking systematically moves exposure from niche to popular, hurting diversity and fairness.
Correct — relevance and creator fairness conflict here, so switching to global demands watching Gini and creator activation as a distribution decision.
Results differ — global compares over a larger candidate set, visibly shifting the distribution.
Global ranking's core impact is exposure distribution (fairness), not just latency; treating it as pure performance misses the fairness risk.

termDefinitions.meaning: local 只在用户自己时间线内打分;global 跨全平台内容统一打分,相关性更高但易偏移曝光分布。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Local ranking scores within a user's own timeline; global scores across all platform content, lifting relevance but skewing exposure.

rows: 内容同质、用户抱怨看不到全站好内容
创作者 Gini 已偏高、需保多样性

scenario: 一个实验显示 +2% CTR,像个明显的赢;但同一实验里创作者激活率 -1.5%。
scenario_en: An experiment shows +2% CTR (a clear win), but in the same experiment creator activation rate drops 1.5%.
q: 为什么必须同时看消费者侧和创作者侧指标?
q_en: Why must you monitor consumer-side and creator-side metrics jointly?
why: 只看消费者侧 CTR 会把它当赢,但创作者激活 -1.5% 说明供给侧生态在受损:创作者流失最终会掏空内容池、反噬长期消费体验。必须双侧联看,才能识破这种「看着赢、实则伤生态」。
why_en: CTR-only reads it as a win, but the -1.5% creator activation shows supply-side ecosystem harm that eventually hollows out content, so both sides must be watched together.
options: 只看 CTR 就够,创作者指标是次要的,+2% 就该上线,不用等创作者侧数据回来
双侧联看:+2% CTR 但创作者激活 -1.5% 说明供给侧受损,长期会反噬消费体验
只看创作者侧就够,消费者 CTR 不重要,消费体验可以先放一边慢慢再看
两侧指标独立无关,一个涨一个跌纯属巧合,和排序策略选择没有任何因果关系
options_en: CTR alone suffices; creator metrics are secondary, so +2% should ship without waiting for creator-side data to come back.
Watch both sides: +2% CTR but -1.5% creator activation signals supply-side harm that later hurts consumer experience.
Creator-side alone suffices; consumer CTR does not matter, so consumer experience can be set aside for later.
The two sides are independent; one up and one down is pure coincidence, with no causal link to the ranking policy chosen.
optionExplanations: 把创作者当次要正是踩坑：创作者流失会掏空内容供给，短期 CTR 赢换来长期崩。
对;消费和创作是同一生态的两端,创作者激活下降预示内容池萎缩,双侧联看才不被单侧假赢骗到。
只看创作者又走另一极端,消费者体验同样是平台命脉,不能偏废。
两者高度耦合:排序偏向刺激性内容常同时抬 CTR、压创作者激活,不是巧合。
optionExplanations_en: Treating creators as secondary is the trap: creator attrition hollows out content supply, trading a short-term CTR win for a long-term collapse.
Correct — consumers and creators are two ends of one ecosystem, and falling creator activation foretells a shrinking content pool, so joint monitoring avoids the one-sided false win.
Creator-only is the other extreme; consumer experience is equally the platform's lifeblood and cannot be ignored.
The two are tightly coupled: ranking toward sensational content often lifts CTR while suppressing creator activation — not coincidence.

termDefinitions.term: consumer-creator joint monitoring / 消费者-创作者联合监控
termDefinitions.meaning: 同时看用户侧 engagement 和创作者侧健康,识破「看着赢实则伤生态」的实验。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Consumer-creator joint monitoring watches user engagement and creator health together to catch experiments that look like wins but harm the ecosystem.

scenario: Staff+ 级答案不满足于「退化就回滚」,而是想让系统在创作者生态受损时自我纠偏。
scenario_en: A Staff+ answer is not content with 'roll back on degradation' and wants the system to self-correct when the creator ecosystem is harmed.
q: 面对创作者激活率持续下滑,Staff+ 会提出什么超越回滚的机制?
q_en: For a sustained drop in creator activation, what beyond-rollback mechanism does Staff+ propose?
why: Staff+ 提反馈回路:创作者激活率持续下滑时,自动触发重新校准目标函数的权重(比如上调创作者公平/多样性项),而不只是回滚到旧模型。这把公平从事后监控变成了目标函数里的闭环控制。
why_en: Propose a feedback loop where declining creator activation triggers re-calibrating the objective's weights (boosting fairness/diversity terms), not just rolling back to the old model.
options: 永远只回滚到旧模型,不改目标函数,下次遇到同样的创作者生态问题还会再退化
反馈回路:创作者激活持续下滑时自动重校目标函数权重(上调公平/多样性项),而非只回滚
直接关闭个性化排序,退回时间倒序,牺牲相关性也没解决目标函数权重失衡的问题
给所有创作者发放固定补贴,和排序目标解耦,治标不治本,权重照样失衡
options_en: Always just roll back to the old model without changing the objective, so the same creator-ecosystem problem degrades it again next time.
A feedback loop: sustained declining creator activation auto-recalibrates the objective weights (boosting fairness/diversity), not merely rollback.
Turn off personalized ranking and revert to reverse-chronological, sacrificing relevance without ever fixing the imbalanced objective weights.
Give all creators a fixed subsidy, decoupled from the ranking objective, treating the symptom while the weights stay imbalanced.
optionExplanations: 只回滚是把系统拉回旧点,治不了「目标函数本身权重失衡」这个根因,下次照样退化。
对;把创作者激活当反馈信号去闭环调目标权重,让系统在生态受损时自动上调公平项,这才是 Staff+ 的生命周期视角。
关个性化是因噎废食,牺牲了相关性,也没解决目标权重问题。
发补贴是产品/运营手段,不改排序目标,治标不治本,和模型闭环无关。
optionExplanations_en: Rollback only returns to an old point and cannot fix the imbalanced objective weights, so it degrades again next time.
Correct — treating creator activation as feedback that auto-boosts fairness/diversity weights when the ecosystem suffers, not just rolling back — the Staff+ view.
Killing personalization overreacts, sacrifices relevance, and never addresses the objective-weight issue.
A subsidy is a product/ops lever that does not change the ranking objective — symptom relief, unrelated to a model feedback loop.

termDefinitions.term: objective re-calibration feedback loop / 目标校准反馈回路
termDefinitions.meaning: 用生态指标(如创作者激活)作反馈,自动上调目标函数里的公平/多样性权重,而非只回滚模型。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An objective-recalibration feedback loop uses ecosystem metrics like creator activation to auto-adjust fairness/diversity weights in the objective, beyond rollback.

scenario: 一场病毒事件让某一类内容(比如短视频)在几小时内暴增刷屏,排序质量随之走样。
scenario_en: A viral event floods one content type (say short video) within hours, and ranking quality warps.
q: 这属于哪类根因,为什么离线评估没提前抓到?
q_en: Which root-cause category is this, and why did offline evaluation miss it?
why: 属于数据分布漂移:线上输入分布突然偏离训练时的分布,模型没见过这种内容配比,预测失准。离线评估用的是历史静态数据,抓不到「未来才会出现的病毒式分布突变」,只能靠线上分布漂移监控发现。
why_en: It is data distribution shift — live input suddenly diverges from training — and offline evaluation on static historical data cannot foresee a future viral spike, so only online drift monitoring catches it.
options: 特征管线故障,因为特征值全变 null 了,是上游数据源或 ETL 挂了导致的
数据分布漂移:输入分布突变偏离训练分布;离线用历史静态数据,抓不到未来的病毒式突变
模型回归,因为训练脚本写错了,某次训练跑出了更差的权重却通过了离线评估
网络故障,因为流量太大打满带宽,是基建可用性问题而不是模型质量问题
options_en: Feature-pipeline failure, because all feature values turned null — the upstream data source or ETL job went down.
Data distribution shift: input distribution spikes away from training; offline uses static historical data and cannot foresee a future viral surge.
Model regression, because the training script had a bug and one run produced worse weights that still passed offline evaluation.
Network failure, because traffic saturated the bandwidth — an infra-availability problem, not a model-quality one.
optionExplanations: 特征没缺失,值是好的,只是内容配比变了,不是 null 问题。
对;病毒事件改变了输入分布,模型在训练时没见过这种配比;离线静态数据无法预见未来突变,得靠线上漂移监控。
训练脚本没错,模型本身是好的,退化来自世界变了不是模型坏了。
带宽满是基建可用性问题,和排序质量因分布突变而走样是两回事。
optionExplanations_en: Features are not missing; values are fine — the content mix changed, not a null problem.
Correct — the viral event changed the input distribution the model never saw in training; static offline data cannot foresee it, so online drift monitoring is needed.
The training script is fine and the model is good; degradation is from the world changing, not a broken model.
Saturated bandwidth is an infra-availability issue, distinct from ranking quality warping from a distribution spike.

termDefinitions.term: viral distribution shift / 病毒式分布漂移
termDefinitions.meaning: 突发热点让某类内容短时暴增,线上输入分布偏离训练分布,模型预测失准。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A viral distribution shift is a burst that floods one content type, moving live input off the training distribution and skewing predictions.

scenario: 同样是「设计 feed 排序的 serving 与监控」,L4 和 L5 答案差在哪。
scenario_en: For the same 'design feed-ranking serving and monitoring', how do L4 and L5 answers differ?
q: L5 答案比 L4 多了哪些关键要素?
q_en: What key elements does an L5 answer add over L4?
why: L4 泛谈 fan-out+缓存、点名 CTR/延迟,没有显式预算或自动回滚。L5 给出带明确预算(50/50/100ms)的三段式、写放大推理的混合 fan-out、含 KL 回滚的监控栈。
why_en: L4 vaguely names fan-out plus caching with no explicit budget or auto-rollback, while L5 gives budgeted staging (50/50/100ms), write-amplification-reasoned hybrid fan-out, and a monitoring stack with KL rollback.
tradeoff: L4(泛谈组件、serving 与监控分离) vs L5(显式预算、写放大推理、KL 回滚、护栏接告警)
options: L5 只是把 L4 的图画得更漂亮、配色排版更整齐一点,内容没有实质区别,面试官根本分不出高下
L5 加了显式延迟预算的三段式、按写放大推理的混合 fan-out、含 KL 回滚触发的监控栈、护栏接生产告警
L5 只多讲了用哪种编程语言、哪个前端框架去实现具体细节,和架构推理深度、取舍判断完全无关
L5 去掉了监控栈,专注把模型参数做得更大更贵,反而比 L4 讲得更少更空洞,监控闭环整个消失不见了
options_en: L5 just draws L4's diagram more nicely with tidier colors and layout, no substantive difference, and an interviewer could not tell them apart at all.
L5 adds budgeted three-stage pipeline, write-amplification-reasoned hybrid fan-out, a monitoring stack with KL rollback triggers, and guardrails wired to production alerting.
L5 only adds which programming language and frontend framework implement the details, entirely unrelated to architectural reasoning depth or trade-off judgment.
L5 drops the monitoring stack and focuses on making the model parameters bigger and pricier, ending up saying even less and emptier than L4, monitoring gone.
optionExplanations: 差别是实质性的推理深度,不是画图好看:L5 把每个选择的预算和触发条件都讲清了。
对;L5 的加分点是显式预算、写放大量化、自动回滚触发、护栏与告警联动,体现端到端的工程闭环。
语言选型不是分级依据,面试考的是架构推理与权衡。
L5 恰恰强化了监控(KL 回滚、护栏告警),不是去掉它。
optionExplanations_en: The gap is substantive reasoning depth, not prettier diagrams: L5 spells out each choice's budget and trigger.
Correct — L5's plus points are explicit budgets, quantified write amplification, auto-rollback triggers, and guardrail-alerting integration, showing an end-to-end loop.
